hero.title: Your AI Safety career starts here.
hero.body: AI Safety expertise has never been more important than today. SAIN provides the community, courses and resources to help students and professionals join the AI Safety field. We provide a clear path through education, community and practical projects, then connect strong contributors to the organisations, programmes and roles where they can take the next step.

meta.title: About
meta.description: Stichting Safe AI Netherlands develops the talent the Netherlands needs to address the risks of transformative AI. The talent pipeline, the foundation documents, and the people who run it.

mission: Develop the talent the Netherlands needs.
Address the risks of transformative AI.
Make a first real contribution possible.
hero.body: That is the mission of Stichting Safe AI Netherlands. Transformative AI could reshape the economy, science, and society on the scale of a major historical revolution; whether that goes well is not decided yet. We are a national talent pipeline: local chapters on shared infrastructure, from first contact through courses and the Project Hub, with a handoff into the wider field. This page shows that path, what we have written down, and the people who run it.

path.heading: The Netherlands has the talent. It lacked the path.
paragraphs: On the current trajectory, AI systems may soon do most economically and strategically important cognitive work, including AI research itself. The critical question is not only what AI will become, but whether enough people are ready to shape what happens next. Right now, far too few are working on that problem.

Nobody can name the exact timeline, and we will not pretend to. Readiness is not something the Netherlands has by default. It is something people build, while European institutions are staffing their AI safety functions in the next few years.

The Netherlands has world-class universities, ASML at the centre of the global semiconductor supply chain, proximity to Brussels, and emerging AI safety groups. What it lacked was a unified civil-society voice and a clear path from interest to capability to meaningful contribution. SAIN was created to close that gap. We develop the people; the field puts them to work.

pipeline.heading: Anyone can start. The path narrows as you grow.
paragraphs: The Funnel Diagram is the whole organisation. The wide end is a free course anyone can join, no technical background required. The narrow end is full-time work on AI safety, in policy, research, industry or civil society. Between them sit the community, the Project Hub, and fellowships. Progress through it is visible, to us and to the person making it, and SAIN’s job is to make each next step reachable, so that every step someone takes compounds into a more effective mission.

We are open about where our effort goes. SAIN builds the wide end: getting people in, teaching foundations, and scaffolding a first real contribution such as a supervised research project. At the narrow end we mainly connect and refer, with introductions and referral letters.

We designed the pipeline with many good endings. Someone who takes one course and returns to law, medicine or public administration carries that knowledge into their profession, and a society fluent in AI risk is an outcome we actively want.
pipeline.record: So far the pipeline has produced more than 100 course graduates across nine-plus cohorts, currently around 60 a year, and peer-reviewed research at NeurIPS and ICLR. The aim for mid-2027 is 250 or more graduates a year, reached by running the same standardised course in more cities.

team.body: SAIN is led by its national director and the heads of growth, operations and projects. The leadership takes the strategic decisions; the chapters run the courses, events and communities.

documents.heading: The rules we hold ourselves to are public.
documents.body: SAIN is a Dutch foundation, a stichting, the standard nonprofit legal form. The foundation holds the brand, the legal entity and the finances, so a local chapter never has to build those from scratch; chapters run their own courses, events and communities. Every programme is free. Three documents define how the whole thing works, and anyone can read them.
documents.contactLine: Role addresses and chapter contacts live on one page, so they stay accurate.
documents.chapterLine: Want to bring SAIN to your city? Chapters adopt the brand, the legal umbrella and ready-made curricula instead of starting from scratch.

meta.title: Volunteer
meta.description: SAIN runs on volunteers. Six teams across Amsterdam, Utrecht and Groningen, three to ten hours a week, one short application reviewed as it arrives.

hero.heading: SAIN runs on volunteers
hero.body: Every programme is free because people give a few hours a week to run it. This page is the work, what you get from it, and the way in.
hero.photoAlt: People working together at a table during a hackathon

work.heading: Six teams, three to ten hours a week
work.body: Amsterdam, Utrecht and Groningen each run the same teams. Leads carry a team and report to the chapter’s director; team members carry a slice of it. Most roles are three to five hours a week, leads six to ten.

education.name: Education
education.description: Run course cohorts and discussion groups. Facilitate weekly sessions, support participants, and keep quality high across iterations.

events.name: Events
events.description: Plan and deliver the chapter's calendar. Hackathons, expert talks, socials, and the logistics behind them.

communications.name: Communications
communications.description: Writing, design, photography, video and the website. Make the chapter's work visible and on-brand.

community.name: Community
community.description: Welcome new members, be the first point of contact, and help people find their way into deeper involvement.

outreach.name: Outreach
outreach.description: Be SAIN's face on campus. Tabling, flyers, and inviting students to upcoming events.

research.name: Research operations
research.description: Keep the Project Hub running day to day. Onboard researchers and supervisors, track projects, and unblock problems.

work.paidNote: SAIN also hires a small number of paid national staff when a role needs it. Those roles are listed with the open positions.

returns.heading: You leave with work you can point to
returns.body: Volunteer roles at SAIN carry real ownership early. Leads report straight to chapter directors, and team members run cohorts, events and channels that actually happen. You work alongside people across Utrecht, Groningen and Amsterdam who are moving into the field themselves, and many of the introductions that matter later start here.
items: Experience with real responsibility, not shadowing
A network across three chapter cities
A track record in the field: cohorts taught, events run, work published

apply.heading: One short application, reviewed as it arrives
apply.body: All chapter applications go through the same short form: name, CV, and a one-page motivation letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so apply whenever you are ready.

steps.title: Apply.
steps.body: Pick the chapter and the role, attach your CV, and write a short motivation letter. One page is plenty.

steps.title: Hear back.
steps.body: We read applications as they arrive. First response within 2 to 3 weeks.

steps.title: Talk.
steps.body: A 30 to 45 minute call about the role, your motivation, and a small task or scenario relevant to the team.

steps.title: Start.
steps.body: If that goes well, onboarding begins with the next cycle, and joining at other dates is possible.

apply.noRoleFits: No role that fits? Apply anyway. Tell us what you want to do in your motivation letter, and we will figure out together what works well for you.

close.body: A few hours a week, a team in your city, and applications reviewed on a rolling basis. The next cohort of courses, events and research support gets run by whoever joins now.

volunteers.heading: SAIN is run by volunteers
volunteers.body: Most of the roles on this page are volunteer roles, taken on by people who want AI to go well and have three to ten hours a week to give to that beside their studies or job. You would run a course, a chapter’s events or its communications, with a team around you and a chapter that counts on you. Many of the people who started this way now work on AI safety at labs, institutes and ministries, and a role here is often the first entry on that CV.

fundamentals.whoItSuits: For newcomers. Taught so you can drop in for any theme, no background needed.
fundamentals.summary: A weekly series on risks, technical safety and governance, taught so newcomers can drop in. Three editions in Utrecht have reached more than 100 students, researchers, engineers and public-sector people.

Pathways: thesis, fellowship, then a full-time role

cadence.heading: How cohorts run
cadence.body: Not sure which chapter fits? Each city’s page lists its own programmes in detail.
rows: Cohorts run per chapter. Groningen and Amsterdam teach in six-week blocks, and Groningen runs three to four cohorts a year. Utrecht's Technical AI Safety and AI Governance blocks run four weeks.
The six-week courses pair weekly readings with an on-site discussion session.
AI Safety Fundamentals in Utrecht is weekly and modular. Drop in for any theme, about 60 minutes.
Some programmes are application-based and close per cohort. The Amsterdam BlueDot tracks are an example.
One form covers participants and facilitators. Facilitator deadlines close a few days earlier.

startChapter.heading: The next chapter starts with one meetup.
startChapter.body: No chapter in your city yet? The three that exist all started the same way: a few people who wanted a local AI safety community and were willing to host the first meetup. SAIN’s leadership guides founders through the whole process, and new chapters operate under the national stichting, so no separate legal entity is needed.

Set up your local channels and your chapter page on this site.
Do the first outreach and run the first meetup.
When you are ready, run a first course; the curriculum and guides are part of the kit.
